**No. There is still substantial work I can do with the material already available.** The last ZIP completed a **targeted six-correction pass**, not an exhaustive review of everything here. I should have made that distinction clearer. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="0"}

## Work that does not need to wait for Codex

I checked the original :chatgpt-content-reference{index="5"}[handoff archive](sandbox:/mnt/data/DD_Continuation_05_Handoff_03.zip). It already contains these five additional full packages; their nested archive hashes match their bindings and their ZIP integrity checks pass.

| Available package | Work still possible now |
|---|---|
| **Rank8Damage6** | Conduct the six-spell source conference, address its **20 explicit questions**, and prepare source-linked decisions, necessary procedures and test cases. |
| **Rank7IdentityCasting5** | Conduct the five-spell conference and address its **24 explicit questions**, retaining actual class access and source-specific restrictions. |
| **Copied-feat release integration** | Review the existing commitment/release implementation against its accepted contracts and the newly drafted Ready correction. Identify necessary changes without reopening settled rules. |
| **Copied-feat recipient effects** | Review the supplied health, buff and movement integrations for transaction ordering, lifecycle, cleanup and source-specific interactions. |
| **Copied-feat class providers** | Review the actual Shaman and Mirrorsage integrations, including resource ownership, concentration and shared allowances. Check them against the new cross-round Ready choice without assuming that choice is already implemented. |

**That includes 11 additional spell identities with 44 unanswered conference questions**, plus the three implementation-evidence packages. Their presence makes them available for review—not automatically correct or accepted.

There is also further work on the existing correction package: converting its remaining integration obligations into more complete source-qualified test specifications and checking dependent documents for concrete contradictions. The previous pass supplied **ten integration cases that have not been executed in the actual runtime**. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="1"}

## What actually requires something else

**Closing all of Control15 requires its missing exact source material.** The last pass had the complete draft but only **35 of its 54 bound source files**. That limits whole-cohort acceptance; it does **not** prevent work on other complete packages. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="2"}

**Command Undeath still needs qualifying creature content.** Its accepted procedure does not supply an operative Undead creature with CR exactly 2, so its two positive-case holds cannot be cleared by additional wording or by borrowing a generated summon’s assumed rating. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="3"}

**Production implementation and actual engine validation remain separate.** You reserved implementation for Codex after your instruction. The reference models and checks in my package are specifications, not replacement game-engine code. Human gameplay and numerical balance also remain uncompleted gates. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="4"}

## The next useful sequence

My priority would be to **check the three copied-feat integrations against the new Ready decision first**, because that directly affects the correction package you will hand to Codex. Then proceed through **Rank8Damage6 and Rank7IdentityCasting5**, producing separately bound corrections and decisions.

**You do not need to instruct Codex to implement the last package before that review work continues. The available material has not been exhausted, and the last delivery was a checkpoint—not the end of what can be corrected now.**

items.text:
**I prepared six scoped rules corrections for Codex, with 22 exact before-and-after operations across five source files.** The package includes the complete originals, corrected copies, source references, preserved cases and verification tools. **Nothing was changed in GitHub or the applied project index.**

:chatgpt-content-reference{index="2"}[Download the complete correction package](sandbox:/mnt/data/DD_Part5_Control_Ready_Corrections_01.zip)

:chatgpt-content-reference{index="3"}[Read the correction review](sandbox:/mnt/data/DD_Part5_Control_Ready_Corrections_01/REVIEW.md) · :chatgpt-content-reference{index="4"}[Read the Codex handoff](sandbox:/mnt/data/DD_Part5_Control_Ready_Corrections_01/CODEX_HANDOFF.md)

## What I corrected

| Area | Correction |
|---|---|
| **Mental Prison damage and replacement** | Entry and exit are separate damage events belonging to one original-caster damage root. The exit retains the original Null snapshot rather than recalculating it later. Exit entitlement is consumed before callbacks so duplicate cleanup cannot deal damage twice. Same-caster concentration replacement and different-caster prison replacement now have explicit, different ordering. |
| **Puppet Strings escape timing** | The first scheduled escape save no longer depends on whether a movement order was delivered or executed. Suppression at START, Grappled, zero Speed or an unavailable route cannot erase that END save. An already-underway phase does not count as a future opportunity, and expiry precedes the final save. |
| **Geas permission escalation** | A task admitted as soft control cannot quietly gain permission to consume a full Action when circumstances change. It must use a lawful soft alternative, wait or suspend the currently impossible portion. The original objective and deadline remain intact. |
| **Dominate Monster companion timing** | Added an explicit, spell-specific bridge for genuinely eligible owner-attached creatures: actual owner phases and structural caps, END saves even without an executed order, and save-only timing when no execution phase exists. Transitions cannot manufacture actions, duplicate saves or reset the deadline. |
| **Ordinary Ready target selection** | Resolved the conflict between generic “choose targets at commitment” wording and Ready’s actual contract. Preparation fixes the spell/mode and pays its casting transaction; release selects the legal targets or area and uses the current geometry and recipient state. No second payment or counter window is created. |
| **Copied-feat Ready allowances** | Resolved `COPY-READY-ALLOWANCE-01` across the shared rule, copy-profile contract, affected feat procedures and acquisition mirrors. Preparation and release now have explicit atomic allowance checks, preventing partial charges, duplicate execution and cross-round cap bypasses. |

The full operative wording and exact source pointers are included—not merely these summaries.

### The consequential copied-feat choice

**A copy prepared in one numbered round and released in the next uses the applicable copy allowance in both rounds, but pays RP, components and capture permission only once.**

A same-round release reuses its preparation’s allowance. A next-round release requires that next round’s allowance to remain available. An applicable Mirrorsage shared allowance is checked only when the character actually owns that engine.

This prevents both countered-preparation spam and releasing a delayed copy alongside another copy that would otherwise bypass the round limit. It is explicitly labelled as a **new scoped authoring choice**, not presented as an already-settled rule.

## What remains deliberately open

These corrections **do not approve all of Control15 or all of Feat335**. They resolve the named gaps inside those pending drafts.

Command Undeath still needs a valid operative **Undead creature with CR exactly 2**, so its two whole-case content holds remain. The Dominate Monster fixtures still need their actual qualifying creature profiles. The Puppet Strings fixture’s prior companion grapple still needs a supported opposing ability-check profile; a saving-throw proficiency bonus is not automatically an Athletics modifier.

Creation, the historical Mind Maze mid-resolution premise and the other previously stated holds remain unchanged. The completed Illusion Exact13 and Companion Exact05 acceptances remain independent. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="0"} :chatgpt-content-reference{index="1"}

There is also a documented source limit: the full Control15 draft was available, but only **35 of its 54 bound source files** were available as exact archived bytes. The package identifies all 19 unavailable bindings by filename, expected size and hash. I have not turned this targeted correction pass into a claim that the complete Control15 conference is finished.

## Verification completed

**129 structural, source, pointer, preservation and staging checks passed**, with zero failures. They verify that the operations reproduce the complete corrected files and reverse to the exact original bytes. The staging tool rejects baseline drift, incorrect before-values, repeated forward application and attempts to overwrite its source directory.

**44 isolated specification tests passed**, with zero failures or errors. These exercise the proposed state-machine behavior and the preserved Mental Prison damage arithmetic. **They are not game-engine tests.** Ten additional source-qualified integration cases are supplied for Codex’s actual implementation.

All 30 original Control15 scenarios remain unchanged. Only three current-case explanatory strings were revised, and their complete previous case objects are preserved. Native source/access records, unrelated procedures, existing approval flags and the applied membership counts remain untouched.

## What to give Codex

Give Codex the ZIP and the included :chatgpt-content-reference{index="5"}[implementation prompt](sandbox:/mnt/data/DD_Part5_Control_Ready_Corrections_01/CODEX_PROMPT.txt). The handoff requires it to compare the exact baselines against the actual working tree **before applying anything**. If those files have advanced, it must reconcile the complete successor rather than overwrite later work.

**Archive:** `DD_Part5_Control_Ready_Corrections_01.zip`  
**Size:** **6,704,401 bytes**  
**SHA256:**
```text
449e40d625447b206422d1e1df776952c30e7a34b72157d1e4cded0dc04793b0
```

The finished archive was reopened, passed CRC and safe-member checks, and all **72 manifest-bound files plus the manifest** were verified.

:chatgpt-content-reference{index="6"}[Download the SHA256 sidecar](sandbox:/mnt/data/DD_Part5_Control_Ready_Corrections_01.zip.sha256)

**The two packages we just finished are done with their requested rules reviews. They now need verified repository integration—not another review of the same rules.** What remains is the rest of the spell backlog, several specific unresolved content/design questions, and the broader implementation and gameplay gates. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="0"} :chatgpt-content-reference{index="1"}

## 1. Apply the 24 newly accepted spell identities

| Position | Reviewed | Pending |
|---|---:|---:|
| **Current authoritative index** | **525** | **323** |
| Illusion/Perception14 accepted, awaiting verified application | +14 | −14 |
| Companion/Life10 accepted with content holds, awaiting verified application | +10 | −10 |
| **Projection after both are applied and verified** | **549** | **299** |

That would put this **ordinary-spell review at approximately 65%**, out of 848 identities. **It does not mean the whole video game is 65% finished.** The application must use the actual then-current index, and the content holds survive the count change. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="2"} :chatgpt-content-reference{index="3"}

## 2. Finish the remaining spell conferences

Your latest queue update has **181 pending identities organized into 27 prepared/active groups**, plus **142 ungrouped identities**. That is the pre-application queue: the 24 just accepted are still included in the official pending total until integration.

The prepared backlog includes these major areas:

| Area | Work still awaiting its own completed review |
|---|---|
| **Control and information** | Control15, Information8, Eye of Judgement and their unresolved interactions. |
| **Travel and planar behavior** | Planar Travel6, plus the relevant portal and glyph decisions. |
| **Life, matter and summoned manifestations** | Vitality/Matter10, Soul/Contact6, Ward7 and Manifestation7. |
| **Rank-seven systems** | Mechanics16, Identity/Casting5, Perception5 and Gate/Glyph3. |
| **Rank-eight systems** | Damage6, Resource6, Control5, Ward5 and Memory/Control4. |

Those are **prepared review packages, not accepted rules**. The newest Ward5 and Memory/Control4 summaries do not replace reading their complete submissions.

The remaining work also includes bringing the ungrouped spells through source reconciliation, necessary decisions, complete procedures and cases. Previously accepted interfaces should be reused throughout; they should not keep becoming fresh debates.

## 3. Resolve the actual holds—not the already-settled rules

**Command Undeath needs valid creature content.** Its procedure is accepted, but no supplied operative creature qualifies as **Undead with CR exactly 2**. Consequently, both positive scenarios, `IN6-09-A` and `IN6-09-B`, remain blocked. This is one underlying content gap affecting two cases—not a reason to redo the other nine Companion procedures. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="4"}

**Mental Prison and the rest of Control15 remain pending.** True Seeing’s conditional interaction does not approve Mental Prison itself. **Creation** remains a separate material/crafting/economy review. **Blink** also remains an unaccepted, receipt-only entry in the current pending count. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="5"}

**The historical mid-resolution Mind Maze example still lacks an established interrupt source.** Its ordinary after-attack Ready case is settled. We do not need to invent an interrupt just to turn the preserved conditional example into an executable encounter. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="6"}

The earlier development handoff also leaves **full Ready transactions, the outstanding copied-feat Ready allowance discussion, full class capture/Echo casting, and world/runtime integration** open. The narrower integrations already reviewed do not close those entire systems.

## 4. Finish the game beyond authored spell rules

The larger campaign-candidate review still needs demonstrated closure across classes and progression, equipment/crafting/economy, creatures and encounters, exploration, factions, onboarding and player/developer presentation. That does **not** mean nothing has been done in those areas; it means the spell acceptances cannot stand in for their completion.

Then the accepted behavior must be implemented and exercised in the actual game: executable state-transition tests, cross-system regression tests, playable encounters, human gameplay testing and numerical balancing. Source hashes and preserved examples support that work, but they do not substitute for it. Cosmology, the 75-domain closure review and release approval remain separate. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="7"}

**My next priority would be Control15 while Codex applies and verifies the two accepted packages.** It addresses a live dependency left by the Illusion review. After that, continue through the prepared conferences rather than repeatedly reopening completed cohorts.

**Bottom line: 24 spell identities are now awaiting integration; approximately 299 others remain afterward, plus the explicit holds and broader game-development work.**
